chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If a muʾadhdhin were to repeat in the two shahadahs, and in ḥayya ʿalā al-salat or ḥayya ʿalā al-falāḥ, two times, three times, or more than that, if by it he only intends the group of people so as to gather them, there would be no harm in it.

key_terms.الشَّهَادَتَيْنِ: the two testimonies of faith in the adhan
key_terms.جَمَاعَةَ الْقَوْمِ: the group of people intended to be assembled
key_terms.حَيَّ عَلَى الصَّلَاةِ: the call inviting people to salat (prayer)
key_terms.حَيَّ عَلَى الْفَلَاحِ: the call inviting people to success in the adhan
key_terms.لَمْ يَكُنْ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: there is no harm or objection in it
key_terms.مُؤَذِّنًا: the one who calls the adhan

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for the muʾadhdhin to repeat parts of the adhan to gather people?
ai.summary: This hadith states that there is no problem if the muʾadhdhin repeats certain phrases of the adhan more than the usual count when the purpose is to gather the people. Its significance is a legal allowance in the practice of worship when repetition serves the communal benefit of assembling the congregation.
